functionEntry.name: probeName
functionEntry.documentation: What rung n is testing, for the log.

functionEntry.name: probePayload
functionEntry.documentation: Rung n itself. Deliberately not a Dictionary until rung 3.

functionEntry.name: <globals/SessionState/<>announceReady>
functionEntry.documentation:
Tell the phone what state the watch is in. Sent on start and in answer
to hello or ping, so the phone modal can show something truthful while
the receiver is still converging.

functionEntry.name: onTransmitResult
functionEntry.documentation: Transmit finished. Only now is a point genuinely delivered.

functionEntry.name: pendingResult
functionEntry.documentation: SEND_PENDING while in flight, then SEND_SENT or SEND_QUEUED.

functionEntry.name: startSession
functionEntry.documentation:
Called once from AppBase.onStart. The receiver comes up immediately, so
that by the time the user reaches the first tree, or the phone sends its
first request, the fix has already converged.

functionEntry.name: linkWarning
functionEntry.documentation:
Only ever shown when something is wrong. A badge that is true on every
screen stops being read; the moment it stops being true is what matters.

functionEntry.name: <globals/SessionState/<>backoffMs>
functionEntry.documentation: How long to wait after a failed send: 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, then 30s.

functionEntry.name: onPhoneCommand
functionEntry.documentation: Dispatch for inbound parcels. See PhoneLink for the protocol.

functionEntry.name: tick
functionEntry.documentation:
Called from every view's render timer. Cheap by design: it reads the
receiver, refreshes the link view and pushes at most one parcel.

functionEntry.name: requestSend
functionEntry.documentation:
Record a point and start it on its way.

Returns SEND_PENDING when the point is on the wire, in which case the
caller polls pendingResult(). Returns SEND_REJECTED immediately when
there is nothing to send, which is the only case the watch refuses: not
a quality judgement, just the absence of a position.

functionEntry.name: <globals/SessionState/<>pump>
functionEntry.documentation:
Move one point off the outbox if the link is free and it is time to try.

The backoff is not politeness, it is the difference between a failed
send and a dead simulator. Without it, a transmit that reports failure
is retried on the very next tick, 40 ms later, and hammering a broken
socket takes the whole process down with "Socket Error in packet
header". One failure is a problem; sixty a second is a crash.

functionEntry.name: endSession
functionEntry.documentation:
Called from AppBase.onStop. Releasing the receiver here is not optional:
Connect IQ never switches it off on its own.

functionEntry.name: <globals/SessionState/<>servePhoneRequests>
functionEntry.documentation:
Do the work the phone asked for, on our own schedule.

Deliberately never called from onPhoneCommand. Transmitting from inside
the receive callback re-enters the comms stack, and that is the most
likely cause of the simulator crash on the tethered link. At most one
parcel leaves per tick.

functionEntry.name: isRemoteActive
functionEntry.documentation: True while the phone, rather than the watch button, is driving.

functionEntry.name: clear
functionEntry.documentation:
Wipe the outbox. Called when a session ends with everything delivered,
so a later session does not inherit stale chunk indices.

functionEntry.name: push
functionEntry.documentation:
Append a point. Returns false when the queue is full, which the caller
should surface rather than swallow: silently dropping field data is the
one thing this app must never do.

functionEntry.name: peek
functionEntry.documentation: The oldest point, without removing it.

functionEntry.name: pop
functionEntry.documentation: Drop the oldest point, once the phone has acknowledged it.

functionEntry.name: <globals/CaptureView/<>setRate>
functionEntry.documentation:
Drop to a slow tick when nothing is moving. The receiver is already the
expensive thing running; the screen should not add to it.

functionEntry.name: requestSend
functionEntry.documentation: Called by the delegate when the user presses to send.

functionEntry.name: onStart
functionEntry.documentation:
Start the receiver and the phone link before any view exists, so the app
is useful the moment it is on screen. When the phone launches this
remotely with openApplication(), this is the first thing that runs.

functionEntry.name: onStop
functionEntry.documentation:
Release the receiver. Connect IQ does not do this for us, and a GNSS
receiver left running is the difference between a working day and an
afternoon.

functionEntry.name: <globals/SummaryView/<>drawQualitySplit>
functionEntry.documentation:
A slim stacked bar: how much of the session was a good fix versus a
merely usable one. Honest, and takes one glance.

functionEntry.name: ringTrack
functionEntry.documentation: Full circle track.

functionEntry.name: signalBars
functionEntry.documentation:
Four ascending bars, filled to match quality. A compact alternative to
the ring for places where the edge is already busy.

functionEntry.name: bitmapCentred
functionEntry.documentation:
Draw a loaded bitmap centred on a point. Used for the TreeMapper mark,
which is a real asset rather than code art so it matches the phone app
exactly. Load it in onLayout and keep it: loading a resource inside
onUpdate is expensive.

functionEntry.name: dot
functionEntry.documentation: Small filled dot, used for status indicators.

functionEntry.name: cross
functionEntry.documentation: Animated cross, for a rejected capture.

functionEntry.name: caption
functionEntry.documentation: Centred caption text.

functionEntry.name: hairline
functionEntry.documentation: A thin horizontal rule, used to separate a hint from the content above.

functionEntry.name: check
functionEntry.documentation: Animated tick. progress 0.0 to 1.0 draws the stroke on.

functionEntry.name: statusPill
functionEntry.documentation: A status pill: a dot plus a short label, centred on cx.

functionEntry.name: ringProgress
functionEntry.documentation:
Continuous progress arc, clockwise from twelve o'clock.
fraction runs 0.0 to 1.0.

functionEntry.name: ringSweep
functionEntry.documentation:
A single sweeping arc used while searching for a fix. headDeg is the
leading edge in degrees; the tail fades out behind it.

functionEntry.name: ripple
functionEntry.documentation: Expanding rings radiating from a point. Used on capture.

functionEntry.name: ringSegments
functionEntry.documentation:
Four segment ring. Quality is a discrete 0..4 value, so four separate
segments read more honestly than a smooth gauge: the user sees steps,
which is what the receiver actually reports.

functionEntry.name: smooth
functionEntry.documentation:
Turn on anti aliasing where the device has it. Guarded, because it
arrived in API 3.2.0 and older products will throw Symbol Not Found.

functionEntry.name: spinner
functionEntry.documentation:
A short arc chasing its tail. Used while a point is in flight to the
phone, which is fast but not instant over Bluetooth.

functionEntry.name: nextTree
functionEntry.documentation: Back to the capture screen, ready for the following tree.

functionEntry.name: finish
functionEntry.documentation: End the session and show what was collected.

functionEntry.name: easeInOut
functionEntry.documentation: Ease in out cubic. Good for things that loop.

functionEntry.name: pulse
functionEntry.documentation: A 0..1 triangle wave over the given period, in milliseconds.

functionEntry.name: easeBack
functionEntry.documentation: Overshoot slightly then settle. Used for the capture confirmation.

functionEntry.name: breathe
functionEntry.documentation: A smooth 0..1 breathing wave over the given period.

functionEntry.name: easeOut
functionEntry.documentation: Ease out cubic. Fast start, gentle settle. Good for things arriving.

functionEntry.name: <globals/PhoneLink/<>stripNulls>
functionEntry.documentation:
Copy a payload without its null values.

A null inside a Dictionary has to survive serialisation into a Java Map
on the other side of the link, and that path is a prime suspect for the
simulator crash seen on the tethered connection. An absent key and a
null value mean the same thing to the phone, so drop them.

functionEntry.name: isBusy
functionEntry.documentation:
True when a transmit is already in flight. The caller should wait
rather than stacking sends.

functionEntry.name: sendRaw
functionEntry.documentation:
Transmit a payload of any type, skipping the Dictionary-only handling.

Only the probe ladder in Probe.mc needs this: transmit accepts a String,
a Number and an Array as well as a Dictionary, and knowing which of
those the tethered transport survives is the whole point of the ladder.
Everything else goes through send().

functionEntry.name: hasHeardFromPhone
functionEntry.documentation:
Heuristic: the phone app has spoken to us recently. Used to distinguish
"no phone" from "phone there, app closed", which are different problems
with different fixes for the user.
Has the companion app ever sent us anything in this session?

functionEntry.name: start
functionEntry.documentation:
onCommand is invoked with the parsed inbound Dictionary.
onSent is invoked with a Boolean, true when the last transmit landed.

functionEntry.name: <globals/PhoneLink/<>unwrap>
functionEntry.documentation: Find the payload dictionary in whatever the phone sent.

functionEntry.name: onTransmitResult
functionEntry.documentation: Called back by the transmit listener.

functionEntry.name: isPhoneConnected
functionEntry.documentation:
Whether a phone is paired and in range. This is the Garmin Connect
link, which is the only signal the watch gets. It does not prove that
TreeMapper itself is open, which is why appLikelyListening() exists.

functionEntry.name: send
functionEntry.documentation:
Post one parcel. Returns false when the link is busy or unavailable,
in which case the caller keeps the point in the outbox and retries.

functionEntry.name: textTop
functionEntry.documentation: Vertical centre for a block of text of the given font.

functionEntry.name: markResource
functionEntry.documentation:
Which mark bitmap suits this screen.

The resource compiler cannot scale a bitmap by a fraction of the screen,
so three sizes ship and the right one is chosen here. Each is about 30
percent of its target screen width.

functionEntry.name: markResourceSmall
functionEntry.documentation: A smaller mark, for the About page.

functionEntry.name: <globals/Layout/<>pickHero>
functionEntry.documentation: The biggest numeric font the screen can carry without crowding the ring.

functionEntry.name: onSelect
functionEntry.documentation:
Skip ahead. The capture screen refuses only when there is no position
at all, so an impatient user cannot break anything here.

functionEntry.name: isMultiBand
functionEntry.documentation: True when this device gave us a multi band solution.

functionEntry.name: <globals/GpsService/<>bestConfiguration>
functionEntry.documentation:
The best GNSS configuration this device actually supports.

Multi band (L1 + L5) is the accuracy win under canopy and the reason
this project exists, so it is asked for first. Every option is gated by
hasConfigurationSupport, because one binary runs on several products and
asking for an unsupported configuration is a runtime error.

SAT_IQ is deliberately not in the list. It trades accuracy for battery
by picking the solution dynamically, which is the opposite of what a
survey tool wants.

functionEntry.name: quality
functionEntry.documentation: Current fix quality, 0 to 4, matching Position.Quality.

functionEntry.name: stop
functionEntry.documentation:
The receiver does not switch itself off. Every exit path must come
through here or the watch quietly burns its battery.

functionEntry.name: warmupSeconds
functionEntry.documentation:
Seconds the receiver has been searching. Shown while acquiring so the
user can tell the difference between slow and broken.

functionEntry.name: snapshot
functionEntry.documentation:
A point ready to put on the wire, or null when the receiver has never
produced a position.

Note what is NOT here: no quality filtering. The watch reports what the
receiver said and lets the phone decide, so `q` travels with every
point and nothing is silently dropped.

`ts` is the GPS timestamp of the fix, not the watch clock. Positions are
dead reckoned between real fixes and then freeze, so the phone needs to
know how old a coordinate is to judge it.

functionEntry.name: blend
functionEntry.documentation:
Linear blend between two 0xRRGGBB colours. t runs 0.0 (a) to 1.0 (b).
This is how every fade in the app is done, since alpha is not available
on older products.

functionEntry.name: quality
functionEntry.documentation: Colour for a Position.Quality value, 0..4.

functionEntry.name: qualityLabel
functionEntry.documentation: Human label for a quality value.

functionEntry.name: fade
functionEntry.documentation: Fade a colour toward the background. 1.0 is fully visible, 0.0 invisible.

functionEntry.name: onBack
functionEntry.documentation:
Back ends the session and shows the summary rather than silently
dropping out. Losing a morning of work to a stray press is the worst
failure this app could have.

functionEntry.name: progress
functionEntry.documentation: Raw 0..1 progress.
